external_entities.name: colleague
external_entities.description: A colleague who signs in through the identity broker and uses applications.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Colleagues sign in to it from wherever they are, including their own devices at home.

external_entities.name: franchise colleague
external_entities.description: A colleague from a franchise store whose own identity provider vouches for them.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Franchise colleagues do not have staff accounts with us; their own identity provider vouches for them

external_entities.name: franchise identity provider
external_entities.description: An identity provider operated by the franchise that vouches for franchise colleagues.
external_entities.source_excerpt: their own identity provider vouches for them and the broker takes that as a sign-in.
external_entities.notes: The source does not state which colleagues this provider is allowed to vouch for.

external_entities.name: HR system
external_entities.description: The HR system that supplies group membership changes and leaver changes overnight.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Group membership is not maintained there by hand — it comes from the HR system overnight.

processes.name: identity broker
processes.description: The broker signs colleagues in, issues tokens, accepts federated sign-ins, and signs tokens for applications.
processes.source_excerpt: Everything colleagues use signs them in through one identity broker.
processes.notes: The source does not state whether colleagues are asked for a second factor.

processes.name: store admin console
processes.description: An application that uses the token's groups to authorize changing prices and voiding transactions across stores.
processes.source_excerpt: The store admin console is one of those applications. It also runs on the corporate network.
processes.notes: The console does not check which store the colleague belongs to, so a store-manager token works against every store.

data_stores.name: key store
data_stores.description: A store holding the signing key used by the identity broker.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The broker signs tokens with a signing key it keeps in a key store.

data_stores.name: directory
data_stores.description: The identity broker's directory of colleagues and their group memberships.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The broker keeps the colleagues and the groups they are in its own directory.
data_stores.notes: Nobody has written down whether the directory is encrypted where it sits.

data_stores.name: audit log
data_stores.description: A log to which the identity broker writes sign-ins.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The broker writes sign-ins to an audit log.
data_stores.notes: Nobody has written down what the log records, whether it covers the franchise route, or whether the log is encrypted where it sits.

data_flows.name: sign-in
data_flows.description: A colleague signs in through the identity broker.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Everything colleagues use signs them in through one identity broker.

data_flows.name: sign-in
data_flows.description: A franchise colleague is admitted through the identity broker using the franchise identity route.
data_flows.source_excerpt: We also let the franchise stores in.

data_flows.name: vouch for colleague
data_flows.description: The franchise identity provider vouches for a franchise colleague to the broker.
data_flows.source_excerpt: their own identity provider vouches for them and the broker takes that as a sign-in.

data_flows.name: issue token
data_flows.description: The identity broker issues a token containing a colleague's staff ID and groups.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Once the broker has signed a colleague in it issues them a token.
data_flows.data_description: token containing staff id and group list

data_flows.name: send token
data_flows.description: The identity broker provides the token used by the store admin console.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every application takes that token and decides what the colleague may do from the groups in it.
data_flows.data_description: token containing staff id and group list

data_flows.name: change prices
data_flows.description: A colleague uses the store admin console to change prices or void transactions.
data_flows.source_excerpt: If the token has the store-manager group in it, the console lets the holder change prices and void transactions.

data_flows.name: fetch public key
data_flows.description: The store admin console fetches the public half of the token-signing key from the broker.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Applications fetch the public half from the broker to check the signature.

data_flows.name: read signing key
data_flows.description: The broker reads the signing key it uses to sign tokens from the key store.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker signs tokens with a signing key it keeps in a key store.

data_flows.name: maintain directory
data_flows.description: The broker reads and updates colleagues and group memberships in its directory.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker keeps the colleagues and the groups they are in its own directory.

data_flows.name: pull changes
data_flows.description: The broker pulls group membership and leaver changes from the HR system overnight.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker pulls the changes once a night, and that is also how leavers stop being colleagues.

data_flows.name: write sign-in
data_flows.description: The broker writes sign-in events to the audit log.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker writes sign-ins to an audit log.
data_flows.notes: The source does not state what the log records or whether it covers the franchise route.

trust_boundaries.name: corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: The corporate network where the identity broker and store admin console run.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The broker runs on the corporate network.

assumptions.assumption: The directory's contents are confidential because they identify colleagues and include their group memberships.
assumptions.basis: The source says the directory keeps colleagues and the groups they are in.

assumptions.assumption: The audit log's contents are confidential because sign-in records can identify colleagues' authentication activity.
assumptions.basis: The source says the broker writes sign-ins to the audit log.

assumptions.assumption: The key store's contents are confidential because it holds the token-signing key.
assumptions.basis: The source says the broker keeps a signing key in the key store.

assumptions.assumption: The store admin console presents a web interface because the source calls it a console.
assumptions.basis: The source names the component 'store admin console'; a console is a web application interface under the extraction rules.
